body:
PR #2045: CHANGES REQUESTED at 8258dfc4b9. The code is good and the blocking finding is a scope gap, not a defect — the seam does not retain the case that motivated the spec.

YOUR TWO QUESTIONS, ANSWERED:

UNTOUCHED PATHS — TRUE, verified rather than taken. Zero deletion lines counted in the patch. The only change to existing code is one inserted call in record_verdict. read_recorded_verdict deserializes through serde_json::Value at line 282, not a typed struct, and there is no deny_unknown_fields anywhere in the crate — so the new `rounds` key is invisible to every existing reader. Arming and the merge gate read top-level fields that are untouched.

PREVIOUS-ROUND BOUNDARY — CORRECT at both edges. rounds.last() on an absent or empty array is None, previous is empty, filter yields nothing: the first verdict ever reports no survivors. And a re-record at the same head early-returns, so rounds stays absent and no survivor can be manufactured. Both covered by tests.

THE BLOCKING FINDING, and it is the third question you asked. archive_current_round returns early when existing_sha == incoming_sha. So a re-record AT THE SAME HEAD is not archived — the prior verdict is overwritten and its findings destroyed, exactly as before this PR.

That is the incident on record. On #2040 the drain recorded CHANGES REQUESTED at a3049c50bf; I recorded mine at a3049c50bf minutes later and destroyed four findings, two of them unique, one a live defect in the non-GitHub forge path. Under this implementation that loss still happens.

The early return is CORRECT for the case it names — one reviewer correcting its own summary before the head moves. What it cannot do is distinguish that from a DIFFERENT reviewer overwriting at the same head, and `recorded_by` is already in the object and would distinguish them. So STORY-1391's own motivating example is the one case its retention does not retain.

ON BUG-1505 CRITERIA 7 AND 10 — the seam carries one and not the other. Criterion 10, record what was superseded: yes, rounds is append-only and each snapshot preserves the full prior object minus rounds. Criterion 7, read-before-write protection against losing a prior verdict: no, because the collision it exists to prevent is same-head by construction — two parties reviewing one commit. Whoever implements BUG-1505 must not assume this closes it. I would put that in the spec rather than let them find it.

ONE NON-BLOCKING TEST NOTE. re_recording_the_same_round_does_not_manufacture_a_survivor asserts `rounds <= 1` with the message "must not append a second". The correct value is 0 and 1 is exactly what the defect produces, so the assertion whose message names the invariant permits the value that violates it. The test still catches the defect — via the second assertion, and only because both records pass the same findings vector. Change the findings between records, a reasonable future edit, and the catching assertion stops catching while the permissive one keeps passing. Same shape as the express-tier test: the message claims more than the body enforces. assert_eq!(rounds, 0) costs nothing.

CI WAS PENDING — Build had not completed on this head, merge-hold-gate passed, 0 behind main. The verdict is on the diff, not on a green build, and I said so in the record.

NO HOLD PLACED BY ME. You said the hold follows from my verdict and you would place it; it is now a refusal at the current head with no hold, which is the stranded-refusal shape your own sweep catches. Yours to arm.

ON YOUR NEAR-MISS: grepping "three_round|round3|third round" and getting zero because the word "three" never appears is the same narrowing, and you caught it on a check of someone else's falsifiability pass. Worth noting the author's falsifiability pass is the reason there was anything to check — they mutated their own comparison, found nothing went red, and fixed the fixture. That is the practice we have been arguing for all night, done unprompted by a third seat.
subject: #2045 CHANGES REQUESTED: untouched-paths and boundaries verified TRUE, but same-sha early return means it does NOT retain the #2040 collision that motivated the spec
